# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

## Reward mechanics (airline tau2)
- What worked (not yet RESULT-confirmed — mechanism verified from evaluator source): reward = DB_check × COMMUNICATE_check. `reward_basis` defaults to `[DB, COMMUNICATE]`; ACTION is commented out. So a task can have DB=1.0 and still score 0 purely because the agent never states the required fact to the user (COMMUNICATE).
- What didn't (mechanism-refuted, pre-RESULT): editing tools to make action args exact cannot raise reward — ACTION isn't in the basis, and the env's Pydantic FlightInfo ignores extra keys anyway. Do not spend an iteration here.
- Promising but not yet tried: for any task gated on the agent quoting a number (price, refund, balance), the "enriched return" lever (surface the computed value + a ready-to-read sentence from the tool) is the direct fix for the COMMUNICATE term.

## Enriched-return lever (compute delta from payment_history)
- Mechanism: `env_update_reservation_flights` / `_baggages` appends exactly one Payment entry equal to the price difference (positive=charge, negative=refund). Read payment_history length before the write, diff after, sum the new entries → exact `amount_charged`. Additive to the returned dict → blast-radius-safe (never alters DB write or existing keys).
- Applied to flights (T11: delta=−5244) and baggages this iteration; pending RESULT confirmation.

## Safe-guard discipline (blast radius)
- A normalization guard is safe to ship on a shared tool ONLY if its firing condition is the malformed shape itself (e.g. `"dob" not in q and "date_of_birth" in q`). Verified this does not fire on passing task 40's well-formed passenger → env call byte-identical. Rule: never widen a guard to also transform well-formed input.
